verdict.rationale: Flagsmith's Release Pipelines let users define stages with triggers and actions that automatically advance flag rollouts, and can auto-generate change requests on promotion to production. This is a native rule-to-action automation, but it is scoped to flag rollout progression. Scheduled flags are time-based one-off changes, not event triggers, so they do not count as event-driven rules. Missing for 10: documentation of which event types can act as triggers, general-purpose event-to-action rules beyond rollout stages, any custom or outbound actions, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: Define stages that your flags progress through automatically, with triggers and actions that control rollouts to selected environments and audiences.
Release Pipelines can automatically generate change requests when promoting flags to production, eliminating manual effort and streamlining your deployment workflow.
Release Pipelines act as your intelligent release assistant, automating your entire feature flag deployment process.
